subject: Site telemetry opt-out & subprocessor export for EU customers
messages:
From: Jane Bright <jane.bright@brightads.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 8 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick questions on site telemetry & EU opt-outs

Hi Karthik —

We're doing a privacy review ahead of onboarding Redwood for a tagging/analytics integration and have a few items we need clarified before we proceed:

1) Does Redwood Console or the SDK collect any client-side identifiers (cookies/localStorage IDs) from end users by default? Specifically for marketing/analytics telemetry (page views, event pings).

2) Where does telemetry data get stored (region and cloud provider)? Do you support EU-only storage for BrightAds accounts?

3) We need a subprocessor export for any vendor that may touch telemetry data (analytics, logging, crash reporting) — can you provide that in CSV?

4) For EU users, is there a recommended snippet we can use to disable Redwood telemetry automatically when a user has opted out via our consent management platform? Any sample code would help.

We are on a tight timeline for our privacy checklist (RFP stage). Can you loop in whoever owns DPAs/subprocessors?

Thanks —
Jane Bright
Head of Privacy, BrightAds
jane.bright@brightads.com

Attachment: privacy-checklist-snapshot.png (image)
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jane Bright <jane.bright@brightads.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 8 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick questions on site telemetry & EU opt-outs

Hi Jane —

Thanks for the clear list. Putting answers below and attaching a subprocessor export and a small opt-out snippet.

1) Client-side identifiers: By default, the Redwood browser SDK emits anonymous event-level telemetry (page views, latencies, error pings) to power Console metrics. We do NOT drop persistent marketing cookies for third-party advertising; the SDK sets a short-lived client id in localStorage for deduplication of events (TTL ~7d) which you can opt out of. Server-side request metadata (IP, user-agent) may be present unless masked by your frontend.

2) Storage: Telemetry for hosted accounts is stored in cloud regions associated with the account. For EU accounts we support EU-only residency (AWS eu-west-1 / GCP europe-west1). If you need EU-only hosting, we can lock storage region as part of the provisioning.

3) Subprocessor export: attached subprocessors_export_20270308.csv — includes analytics providers, logging and monitoring vendors used by our hosted runtime. Let us know if you need the vendor contact or subprocessors' DPA attachments.

4) Opt-out snippet: attached telemetry-optout-snippet.txt (JS). The snippet calls Redwood.init({telemetry: false}) when CMP indicates no consent for analytics. If you prefer server-side suppression, we can provide an edge-filtering rule to drop telemetry for EU sessions.

Next steps: rishi (cc'd) owns DPA/legal — we'll send a pre-signed DPA and a DocuSign link to finalize. Monica will follow up on data retention settings for EU accounts.

Attaching: subprocessors_export_20270308.csv, telemetry-optout-snippet.txt

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Thanks Karthik — this is helpful. A few follow-ups: 

- The localStorage client id is a showstopper unless it can be suppressed for EU visitors. Can you confirm the SDK can be initialized with telemetry disabled per-page (not just at account level)? We need it at runtime since our CMP runs before some tag injections.

- The subprocessors CSV looks good at a glance. Can we get confirmation that none of those subprocessors replicate raw page-level payloads to non-EU regions? If any do, we need contractual safeguards or the ability to turn them off.

- Also, for the DPA: we prefer an executed copy with a clause specifying controller-to-processor flows for telemetry (BrightAds = controller). Can you send the DPA and a DocuSign link?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — this will feed into legal signoff.

Hi Jane — following up with concrete next steps.

1) SDK runtime opt-out: Confirmed — telemetry can be disabled at runtime per page. The attached telemetry-optout-snippet shows how to call Redwood.init({telemetry:false}) after your CMP resolves. For single-page apps we recommend running the snippet in the CMP callback; for tag-manager setups we can provide a GTM template.

2) Subprocessors & EU replication: We've reviewed the subprocessors list and flagged any vendor that maintains multi-region replication. Per the CSV: LogstoreCo (indexing) has replication enabled by default; if you require, we can route BrightAds telemetry through an EU-only logging cluster (no replication to other regions). We'll include that option in the provisioning note.

3) DPA & DocuSign: rishi has prepared the controller-to-processor addendum that clarifies telemetry is processed per your instructions (BrightAds = controller). Jane — sending DocuSign now: https://app.docusign.com/envelope/1234567890abcdef. Once signed, we'll attach the executed PDF.

4) Retention: For hosted EU accounts we can set default telemetry retention to 90 days. If you need shorter retention for EU users, we can add a custom policy in provisioning.

5) Action items for BrightAds:
   - Please confirm you want EU-only hosting (yes/no).
   - Confirm whether you'd like us to disable replication for LogstoreCo for your account.
   - Sign the DPA link above.

I'll loop in our provisioning team after we get your answers. Happy to set a 30-min call if you want to walk through the snippet and provisioning options.

Thanks,
